title: Footpath — a quarterly about walking and where it takes you
description: Long reads about the paths people walk: to work, to school, along coasts and through cities. Four issues a year, and a letter in between.

sections.title: The long way round.
sections.lede: This issue follows six people who chose the slower route to work, and found the city they had been driving past for years.

media.alt: A figure walking along a canal towpath at dawn, the city skyline faint behind

items.title: Forty minutes on foot, every day, for a year
items.excerpt: A bus driver gave up the bus. What she noticed in the first month, and what she still notices.

items.title: The map that drew itself
items.excerpt: How a city's desire lines, the paths worn across its parks, became its new cycle routes.

items.title: In praise of the school run
items.excerpt: Eleven minutes, twice a day: the most important conversation a parent has is on the pavement.

items.title: Coastline, measured by hand
items.excerpt: A retired surveyor walks the shore of his county and finds it is longer every time.

sections.title: We publish slowly on purpose. A walk takes as long as it takes, and so does a good story about one.

steps.title: Leave early
steps.body: The canal at six, before the cyclists, when the herons still own it.

media.alt: A heron standing on a lock gate in mist

steps.title: Take the cut-through
steps.body: The alley behind the market that every resident knows and no map shows.

media.alt: A narrow brick alley with crates stacked at its far end

steps.title: Arrive on foot
steps.body: Forty minutes later than the car, and somehow less tired.

media.alt: An office door, a pair of muddy boots beside it

sections.text: You only learn a city at the speed of your feet. Everything faster is just the order of the stops.

sections.title: The letter, between issues
sections.body: One email a month: a walk, a map and a story we could not fit in print.
sections.note: No tracking pixels. Leave with one click, from any letter.

footer.note: Footpath is reader-funded and has no advertising.
